task.evidence: 29 May – €16.4 billion of EU funds are unfrozen for Hungary.

The EU funding freeze for Hungary refers to the freezing and suspension by the European Commission of EU funds allocated to Hungary, primarily due to Hungary's backsliding on the rule of law, judicial independence, academic freedom, and democratic norms. EU funding freeze for Hungary
Background
Many EU member states have repeatedly expressed their concerns about the state of rule of law in Hungary under Viktor Orbán. In December 2022, the European Commission froze funds for Hungary due to Hungary's backsliding on the rule of law. In the first decade of the 21st century, Hungary emerged as one of the most successful recipients of EU funds in Eastern and Central Europe.  In January 2025, Ursula von der Leyen wrote a letter to Viktor Orbán promising to unfreeze EU funds for Hungary, after Orbán agreed to drop his opposition to extending sanctions against Russia.




History
Freezing of funds
On December 12, 2022, the EU froze €6.3 billion of the Cohesion Fund allocation for Hungary.
On December 15, 2022, the European Commission suspended €0.55 billion of Hungary's cohesion funds.
On December 13, 2023, the EU released €10.2 billion in funds to Hungary.
On May 29, 2026, the EU unfroze €6.4 billion in funds to Hungary.




Opposition and sanctions
Opposition to EU sanctions on Russia
In early January 2025, Viktor Orbán threatened to veto the extension of EU sanctions on Russia, which would have effectively ended the EU's support for Ukraine."}]
